page.layout: Two woodcut medallion portraits centred at top; below them one column of running text with two paragraphs (the first a biography of Amurathes, the second a short entry on Solimanus); full width. Printed running head at top with page number at left.

main_text.l: AMVRATHES huius nominis primus, Orchanis filius,
mortuo patre, apud Turcas imperat anno mundi 5311. à Chri-
sto nato 1349. Is auitam paternámque felicitatem æmulatus
eft: at vero in Caramanum auum maternum non minus infe-
stus quàm pater fuit, qui socerum occiso eius filio adolescente
non minima Ciliciæ parte exuerat. Cæterùm à Constantinopo-
litano Imperatore Ioanne Palæologo solicitatus Amurathes
12000. Turcarum ei in auxilium mittit: idque initium ac origo
ruinæ imperij Constantinopolitani fuit. Nam Europeis opibus
illectus Amurathes, opis denuo adferendæ simulatione, potiun-
dæ tamen Græciæ animo, Genuensium nauibus vsus Amura-
thes, Thurcarum 60000. in Græciam transportat: Hellespon-
tum ad Abydum superat: Callipolim cum aliis oppidis occu-
pat: in ipsum quoque Imperatorem inexpectato grauem impe-
tum facit. Postea Seruiam, Bulgariamque ingressus, Lazarum
Seruiæ, & Marcum Bulgariæ principes, cum paratissimis copiis
ei occurentes, ingenti cæde profligat, prius occupata Adriano-
poli: sed Lazaro cæso, mox à feruo in domini vindictam Amu-
rathes occiditur, anno regni 23. Vide Egna.lib.2. Pau.Io.& Chri-
stop.Richerium de rebus Turcarum lib.1.
SOLIMANVS Amurathis filius, patri in imperio suc-
cedens, confestim hæreditariæ dignitati eripitur, atque per in-
sidias occiditur à fratre æmulo Baiazete: quamobrem à non-
nullis inter Turcicos Imperatores minimè annumeratur. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits: left labelled "THES TVRC R." and "AMVRA"; right labelled "SOLIMANVS R." and "AMVRAT". Lower-left faint show-through only; not transcribed. Several words in the text are set in a slightly lighter or uneven inking and were read with care; "Amurathes" in the first paragraph and the numerals 5311, 12000, 60000 and 23 are copied as printed (the printed numerals in the original read "5 3 11", "1 2 0 0 0", "6 0 0 0 0" and "2 3"). Where the scan is faint the reading is uncertain but no [?] markers were required.
